question: Prove that $\frac{d}{dx}\left( \int f(x)dx \right) = f(x)$ for any continuous function $f$.
explanation:
Let $F(x)=\int f(x)dx$.

This means $F(x)$ is an anti-derivative of $f(x)$.

By definition of anti-derivative:

$F'(x)=f(x)$.

Therefore differentiating the integral gives:

$\frac{d}{dx}(F(x)+C)=F'(x)=f(x)$.

Hence $\frac{d}{dx}\left(\int f(x)dx\right)=f(x)$.
